title: Hughes files for bankruptcy after GEO business loses ground to Starlink
summary: Hughes, a subsidiary of EchoStar, filed for bankruptcy due to declining geostationary satellite broadband business amid competition from SpaceX's Starlink constellation. The company struggled to maintain its market position against the growing low-Earth orbit broadband service.

title: Xona secures spectrum approval for satellite navigation network
summary: Xona has secured spectrum approval for its satellite navigation network, enabling stronger signal transmission near GPS frequencies. The startup's breakthrough could enhance positioning accuracy and reliability.

title: Airbus and Thales win order for SpainSat replacement
summary: Airbus Defence and Space and Thales Alenia Space have secured a contract to build a replacement military communications satellite for Spain. The deal is part of ongoing efforts to establish a space joint venture involving Airbus, Thales, and Leonardo.
company: Airbus Defence and Space, Thales Alenia Space

title: U.S. Air Force expands Blue Origin rocket cargo contract
summary: The U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory increased Blue Origin's contract by $11.7 million to study the use of space rockets for point-to-point deliveries.

title: Space Force awards K2 Space $22.9 million for laser communications demonstration
summary: The U.S. Space Force has awarded K2 Space a $22.9 million contract to demonstrate laser communications using two satellites equipped with optical terminals for military orbital connectivity.

title: China launches secretive TJS-27 pair, orbits next-gen Tianlian relay sat
summary: China launched a Long March 6A rocket carrying a secretive TJS-27 satellite pair and a next-generation Tianlian relay satellite into orbit. The mission marked an upgrade to China's on-orbit communications relay capabilities.

title: Sending repurposed Mars rover to the moon could cost more than $1 billion
summary: Repurposing a Mars rover for a lunar mission could cost NASA over $1 billion, a figure disputed by the agency's administrator.

title: Spain commits up to $2.3 billion for national military communications for IRIS²
summary: Spain will allocate between €1.6 billion and €2 billion ($1.8 to $2.3 billion) to develop a national military satellite communications constellation as part of the IRIS² program. This investment aims to enhance Spain's secure military communications capabilities.

title: Inside the effort to show Congress what war in space looks like
summary: The Space Force Association’s National Spacepower Center is creating an unclassified environment to demonstrate satellite threats and their impacts on Earth for Congress. This initiative aims to showcase the realities of warfare in space.

title: Space Force picks 15 companies for $981 million training range contract
summary: The U.S. Space Force has selected 15 companies to compete for a $981 million contract to develop satellites, sensors, and systems for realistic military space training exercises. This initiative aims to enhance the Space Force's operational readiness and capabilities.

title: CNN dives into how Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos are backing NASA's race to the moon against China (exclusive clip)
summary: Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos are financially supporting NASA's lunar ambitions as competition with China intensifies. The CNN special 'Eclipsing Power' explores how billionaires influence the global space race.

title: A SpaceX rocket will crash into the moon this week. Why is it on a collision course?
summary: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket's upper stage is set to crash into the moon on Wednesday (Aug. 5). The collision is unintentional and stems from its trajectory after a 2015 mission.

title: Jack in for a cyberpunk jolt with this energized first trailer for Apple TV's 'Neuromancer'
summary: Apple TV has released the first trailer for its upcoming adaptation of William Gibson's 1984 sci-fi novel 'Neuromancer'. This marks a long-awaited proper adaptation of the influential cyberpunk classic.

title: Jupiter's moon Europa may have signs of life in its buried ocean — but can we get to them?
summary: Jupiter's moon Europa may harbor signs of life in its subsurface ocean, raising questions about accessibility for future missions. Scientists emphasize the importance of these findings for guiding future exploration efforts.

title: 3 moons of Neptune may be remnants of ice worlds shattered in a catastrophic crash
summary: Three moons of Neptune may be remnants of ice worlds destroyed in a catastrophic collision. This discovery highlights the need for further exploration beyond Voyager 2's 1989 flyby.

title: The 1st 'three-headed' asteroid | Space photo of the day for Aug. 3, 2026
summary: New images reveal the first-known 'trilobate' or three-headed asteroid in our solar system. Astronomers believe this unique structure provides new insights into asteroid formation.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 3, 2004: NASA launches MESSENGER spacecraft to orbit Mercury
summary: On August 3, 2004, NASA launched the MESSENGER spacecraft to orbit Mercury, aiming to study the planet and search for signs of water. This marked the first mission dedicated to orbiting the innermost planet of our solar system.

title: 13 amazing things to see during the total solar eclipse on Aug. 12
summary: A total solar eclipse on August 12, 2026, will offer unique sights, including the solar corona. The event is expected to provide multiple viewing opportunities.

title: Is the Nocs Provisions Lite View spotting scope a good alternative to a traditional telescope?
summary: The Nocs Provisions Lite View spotting scope is evaluated as a compact alternative to traditional telescopes, offering detailed views of the moon and bright star clusters.

title: Astronomers watch a black hole's feeding frenzy end with a bad case of cosmic indigestion
summary: Astronomers observed a distant black hole's feeding frenzy conclude with a powerful windy outburst. This event marked the end of its intense consumption phase.

title: Louisiana Students Loft Payloads from NASA Balloon Facility in Texas
summary: Louisiana students annually launch payloads from NASA's Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility in Texas to conduct edge-of-space experiments. The initiative provides hands-on learning and data collection opportunities for students and faculty.

title: NASA Delivers Navigation System for Commercial Lunar Relay
summary: NASA delivered the NavCube3-mini payload to Intuitive Machines for integration into the Altus-1 lunar relay satellite, enabling future lunar communications and navigation services for astronauts and rovers.

title: Ike Theriot Helps Prepare Astronauts to Work on the Moon
summary: Ike Theriot leads NASA's Flight Operations Surface Testing team, preparing astronauts for lunar exploration. His journey to NASA involved military service and a strong work ethic.

title: NASA Brings Space Exploration to the FIFA World Cup
summary: NASA hosted a free interactive exhibit at the FIFA Fan Festival in Houston during the World Cup, attracting over 500,000 visitors to showcase space exploration and its benefits to Earth. The exhibit highlighted NASA's Artemis program, Moon Base, and the International Space Station.

title: APOD: 2026 August 3 – Vaporizing Meteor Photobombs the Lacerta Nebula
summary: An astronomy image shows a meteor streaking across the Lacerta Nebula, captured by APOD on August 3, 2026. The photograph highlights the transient nature of meteors in cosmic imagery.

title: APOD: 2026 August 2 – A Fire Rainbow over West Virginia
summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) featured an image of a 'fire rainbow' over West Virginia on August 2, 2026. The phenomenon is explained as being caused by ice crystals in cirrus clouds refracting sunlight.

title: APOD: 2026 August 1 – Buck Moon and Belt of Venus
summary: APOD (Astronomy Picture of the Day) features an image of the Buck Moon and Belt of Venus on August 1, 2026. The post includes an explanation of the celestial event by a professional astronomer.

title: What’s Up: August 2026 Skywatching Tips from NASA
summary: NASA highlights August 2026 skywatching events, including a solar eclipse, the Perseids meteor shower, Venus at its brightest, and a deep partial lunar eclipse.

title: NASA to Host Florida Event Celebrating American Air, Space Leadership
summary: NASA will host a news conference at Kennedy Space Center in Florida on August 14 to preview a new event. The announcement will be held at the XLV Hangar in the Shuttle Landing Facility.

title: Launch Preview: Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions fill launch manifest
summary: The first full week of August is expected to be busy with multiple launches, including Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions. The launch manifest is filled with various space industry activities.

title: Boeing’s Starliner set for potential 2026 cargo run to ISS
summary: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft may conduct a cargo mission to the International Space Station (ISS) in 2026 following redesign efforts. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg highlighted the ongoing modifications to the spacecraft.

title: Starbase Pad 1 Retrofits Progress as Block 3 Flights Start
summary: SpaceX has completed two flights from the newly designed Pad 2 at Starbase while retrofitting work continues on Pad 1. The upgrades are part of preparations for Block 3 flights.

title: Blue Origin continues rebuilding LC-36, prepares testing alternatives for New Glenn second stage
summary: Blue Origin is continuing the rebuilding of Launch Complex 36 (LC-36) and exploring alternative testing methods for the second stage of its New Glenn rocket after a recent pad explosion during a static fire test.

title: Ship 40’s flawless flight promotes next mission catch potential
summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13, featuring Ship 40, successfully completed its mission and returned intact, demonstrating the vehicle's reliability. This achievement paves the way for the next mission, which may involve catching the booster.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9 and Chang Zheng rockets set to launch this week
summary: Five orbital launches are scheduled this week, including a Chang Zheng 6A rocket in China. SpaceX's Falcon 9 is also among the planned launches.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: NASA's Juno mission discovered surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io during two flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the volcanic moon's geology.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to conduct hot-fire tests for the second stage of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket at the Stennis B-2 test stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the New Glenn for its upcoming missions.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones during its third attempt. This marks another successful test for SpaceX's Starship program.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 spacecraft successfully docked at the International Space Station (ISS), bringing three new crew members aboard. A U.S. spacewalk also completed repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of significant contributions by the European Space Agency.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical centre in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission uses a coronagraph to simulate an artificial solar eclipse by blocking the Sun with one satellite to observe the Sun's corona with another. This technique allows for unprecedented studies of the solar atmosphere.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with Europe's space industry on September 16-17 at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technologies for next-generation antennas. These innovations are expected to enhance communication and radar systems in the space industry.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: The European Space Agency's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in ESTEC's Maxwell Test Chamber, ensuring its electronics are fit for space. The mission is scheduled to launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) is hosting events to discuss the implementation of decisions from the CM25 ministerial meeting. These events aim to inform industry about upcoming activities, priorities, and opportunities within ESA programs.

title: True Anomaly Chases an Evading Target
summary: True Anomaly successfully executed the first in-space pursuit of an evading target as part of the VICTUS HAZE mission. This achievement marks a significant milestone in space operations and satellite maneuvering.

title: AFRL Adds $11.7M to Blue Origin’s Point-to-Point Cargo Contract
summary: The U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) has awarded Blue Origin an additional $11.7 million to expand its study on using the company's launcher for point-to-point cargo delivery missions. This funding builds on Blue Origin's existing contract to explore rapid global logistics capabilities.

title: K2 Space Raises $500M Series D at $6.8B Valuation
summary: K2 Space raised $500 million in a Series D funding round, valuing the company at $6.8 billion. This brings K2 Space's total financing to over $1 billion since 2022.

title: NordSpace Funds NVD Amid Canada’s Export Push
summary: NordSpace Ventures invested in North Vector Dynamics, a company developing full-spectrum sovereign missile capabilities. This move aligns with Canada's push to enhance its defense exports.

title: Report: Our Launch Cadence Forecast For Next-Gen Rockets
summary: The article discusses the expected flight cadence ramp for next-generation reusable rockets, including New Glenn, Neutron, Nova, Terran R, and Eclipse. It aims to forecast the launch frequency of these advanced rockets.

title: Payload Field Guide: European Launchers
summary: Europe is rapidly developing new launch capabilities but faces challenges in keeping pace with global competitors. The continent's progress in space launch is highlighted despite slower-than-expected advancements.

title: Hop Aero Wants to Deliver Cargo via Rocket
summary: Hop Aero, a startup launched on Y Combinator, unveiled its autonomous suborbital rocket named Rook, aiming to deliver cargo via rocket. The company is focused on revolutionizing cargo transportation through this innovative technology.

title: Payload Pioneers: Where Are They Now?
summary: The Payload Pioneers program has recognized 90 young professionals in the space industry over three years. The article updates on the current status of some of the 30-under-30 awardees.

title: Outlier Space Raises $7.3M to Build New Zealand’s First Reentry Vehicle
summary: Outlier Space secured $7.35 million to develop New Zealand's first reentry vehicle for microgravity research. The vehicle is planned to debut its first mission in 2028.

title: ESA taps Aalyria to build deep-space network hub
summary: ESA has selected Aalyria to construct a network-operations center for deep-space communication, enabling reliable data sharing among spacecraft across the solar system.

title: Airbus and Thales Alenia Space to Build SpainSat NG-III
summary: Airbus and Thales Alenia Space have been contracted by Hisdesat to build the SpainSat NG-III secure satellite communications satellite for Spain. Airbus will serve as the prime contractor for the project.

title: ETL Acquires Software Developer Amphinicy Technologies
summary: ETL Systems has acquired Amphinicy Technologies, a software developer specializing in satcom and Earth Observation markets. The acquisition aims to enhance ETL's ability to address complex ground segment challenges.

title: Xona Gets Approval to Deploy Commercial Navigation Constellation
summary: Xona has received FCC approval to deploy its commercial navigation constellation called Pulsar, which plans to include more than 250 satellites. The company announced the authorization to broadcast radionavigation signals.

title: Hughes Files for Chapter 11 With Plan to Reorganize Around Enterprise, Defense Business
summary: Hughes Satellite Systems Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection to reorganize around enterprise, defense, and government customers. The move aims to address a decline in consumer business.

title: AccelerCom and Eclipse Space Reveals Details of D2D Collaboration
summary: AccelerComm has completed two engineering engagements with Eclipse Space to define the physical-layer architecture for its next-generation Direct-to-Device spacecraft. The collaboration focuses on advancing sovereign satellite infrastructure.

title: K2 Space Secures Series D Funding After Hitting $1 Billion Contract Value Milestone
summary: K2 Space raised $500 million in Series D funding, valuing the company at nearly $7 billion. The funding follows the achievement of a $1 billion contract value milestone.

title: Hispasat Obtains WTA Certification for Madrid Teleport
summary: Hispasat's Arganda del Rey Teleport in Madrid has received Tier 4 Full certification from the World Teleport Association (WTA), marking the 80th such certification issued. This achievement highlights Hispasat's commitment to high-quality teleport operations.

title: Planet Labs Wins One-Year Agricultural Data Contract with the Scottish Government
summary: The Scottish Government awarded a one-year, seven-figure contract to Planet Labs for agricultural data via its Computacenter reseller. The deal involves Planet Labs' German subsidiary based in Berlin.

title: Fortastra and Hadrian Sign National Security Spacecraft Manufacturing MoU
summary: Fortastra and Hadrian have signed an MoU to collaborate on building advanced spacecraft for national security missions. The partnership aims to address urgent space-based security needs through technical collaboration.

title: Sophia Space and Caltech File Orbital Data Centers Patent
summary: Sophia Space and Caltech have been issued a patent for space-based data centers. The patent, filed in 2024 and issued in 2026, covers architectures for large-scale, modular orbital data centers.
